data.description:
## Why
c11 cannot say how long it was in the foreground. A 5.5-day 0.67 session (1,208 tabs, 110 peak open) was analyzed post hoc on 2026-10-06. Foreground time was unrecoverable: the event log has no app activation or screen-lock signal, and macOS Screen Time is TCC-protected. The best proxy, clustered workspace switches, gave only a lower bound (88 bursts, about 37 h). `last_seen_at` and `c11 history` (1.0) already compute "c11 frontmost, screen unlocked" internally but never emit the edges.

## Deliverable
Add operator-presence events to the event log, driven entirely by notifications c11 already observes or can observe for free:
- `app.activated` / `app.deactivated` (NSApplication didBecomeActive / didResignActive)
- `screen.locked` / `screen.unlocked` (the session resign/become-active notifications, plus the distributed screen-lock notifications)
- `system.sleep` / `system.wake` (NSWorkspace willSleep / didWake)
- `window.occlusion` with `{window_id, visible}` on occlusion-state change, if it is already observed for App Nap handling

Payloads are structural only. Update the envelope schema, `references/events.md`, and the skill, then sync installed skills.

## Performance constraint (hard)
Notification-driven only, with no timers and no polling. Each event goes through the existing EventLog serial queue, so emission is off-main and non-blocking. Nothing touches the typing path, `hitTest`, or `forceRefresh`. Expected volume is tens of events a day.

## Acceptance
1. A real tagged build switched away from and back to c11, then locked and unlocked, writes the paired events in seq order.
2. An offline consumer can compute foreground hours for an instance from the log alone. Add a small helper or `c11 report` section (see the report ticket).
3. A test through the real EventLog path, not a source-text assertion.

data.to:
## Why
A post-hoc analysis of a 5.5-day 0.67 production session (2026-10-01 to 10-06: 1,208 panels created, 110 open at peak, 37 agents working at once, about 32.7B tokens on the host) answered most questions from the event log but hit hard gaps:
- **Foreground time was unknowable.** There is no app-active or screen-lock signal, and macOS Screen Time is TCC-protected.
- **Closed workspaces lost their names.** 51 of 56 workspaces had no title anywhere in the log. Separately, 3 panels restored at launch disappeared with their workspace without any `panel.closed`, so replay showed them open forever.
- **Tokens could not be attributed to panels.** All tokens were known in aggregate, but none could be tied to a panel.
- **Hangs carried no context.** Correlating 41 hang precursors with load required replaying the whole log.
- **Most of the log was spinner frames.** 59% of `metadata.changed` events were spinner title updates, and the log keeps only one rolled 8 MB generation. Absorbed from C11-232.
- **No tool exists.** The analysis was hand-written Python.

## Principles
1. **Log each edge once; derive everything else offline.** The app writes only small structural edges. Summaries, joins, and token math happen in the CLI process, never in the app.
2. **Net-negative cost.** The log-volume reduction from title coalescing must outweigh everything added here, so a 1.1 build writes fewer bytes than 1.0 for the same workload.
3. **Local only.** Nothing here leaves the Mac. This is separate from the existing "Send anonymous telemetry" (Sentry) setting.

## Scope

### App side (small)
1. **Presence edges**, notification-driven only: `app.activated` / `app.deactivated`, `screen.locked` / `screen.unlocked`, `system.sleep` / `system.wake`. Expect tens of events a day. This makes foreground time computable.
2. **Workspace edges** (nice-to-have, keep only if it stays this small): `workspace.created {title, root_directory}`, `workspace.renamed {title, prior}`, `workspace.closed {title}`. When a workspace is torn down, one helper emits `panel.closed` for every id still in `lastKnownPanelIds` (`Workspace.reconcilePanelEvents`), then `workspace.closed`. That one helper also fixes the restore ghosts. If restore teardown can't route through it cleanly, ship the events without the ghost fix.
3. **Title coalescing** (from C11-232): spinner-only OSC title changes, where the title differs only in leading spinner or status glyphs, are not emitted. A panel's title churn is capped to the first and last change plus a count per window.
4. **Retention** (from C11-232): keep several generations, bounded by age (default 14 days) and by total size (default 64 MB). Rolled files are plain renames; no compression on the write path.
5. **Health context:** `hang.precursor` gains `app_active`, `screen_locked` and `rss_mb`. A new `instance.sample {rss_mb, cpu_s_total, threads}` fires every 10 minutes and at clean shutdown. Panel and agent counts are not sampled, because the CLI derives them by replay.
6. **Settings.** Add a "Local activity history" section next to the anonymous-telemetry toggle, with the copy "stays on this Mac":
   - **Record usage analytics** (default on): presence edges, health samples and workspace edges. Off means those emits are skipped at the source.
   - **Keep message and input text** (default on): off records byte counts only for `panel.input_sent` and mailbox bodies. Messages view then shows "text not recorded".
   - **Keep history for** 7 / 14 / 30 days.

   A full kill switch for the log stays a `defaults` key, not UI, because Messages view, mailbox receipts and `c11 feed` read the log. The skill documents what stops working with it off. New strings are localized into all six languages.

### CLI side (zero app cost)
7. **`c11 usage [--since] [--by panel|workspace|model|harness] [--json]`.** It reads Claude Code and Codex transcripts in the CLI process and joins them to panels through the lifecycle journal, which already stores `tab_id`, `session_id`, `agent_kind`, `model_id` and `workspace_id` per event. Claude is deduplicated by message and request id; Codex uses `total_token_usage` deltas. Usage that can't be attributed is reported as unattributed, never dropped.
8. **`c11 report [--instance|--since] [--format md|json]`.** Offline session analytics: span, panels created and peak open or working, agent-hours, lifetimes, workspaces and topics, daily table and hour-of-day rhythm, foreground time, hang rate by load bucket, and tokens via `c11 usage`. It follows the journal's honesty rules: unknown is not zero, and coverage gaps stay visible. Prototype: `~/Projects/Stage11/ideation/c11-session-analytics/scripts/`.
9. **Price catalog:** add the current models (Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Fable 5.1, the gpt-6 family) plus `cache_read_usd` and `cache_write_usd`. A missing price reads "unknown", never zero.

### Out of scope
- Per-keystroke telemetry, or anything on the typing path.
- Panel and agent counters inside the app.
- Closed-panel summary payloads (derived offline instead).
- Sending anything off the machine.

## Performance contract (hard gate)
The target is an operator on a base-model MacBook Air with 8 to 16 GB, not Hyperion.
- **No new main-thread work.** The only new main-thread work is building a small dictionary at notification and lifecycle callbacks that already run there, a few times an hour. Serialization and writes stay on the existing EventLog serial queue (`EventLog.append`), which is fire-and-forget and bounded by `maxPending` with `log.dropped`.
- **Nothing on hot paths.** Nothing touches `hitTest`, `forceRefresh`, `TabItemView`, socket telemetry fast paths, or any per-keystroke path.
- **One new timer.** The 10-minute `instance.sample` is coalesced (leeway of 60 s or more), runs on the log queue, makes one `task_info`/`getrusage` call, and is suspended across sleep.
- **Off is free.** Disabled emits return at the existing `EventEmitter.emit` guard before any envelope is built. Settings are read once per change, not per event.
- **Disk is bounded.** The 64 MB default cap applies across all generations.

**Gate:** run a scripted A/B on a tagged build with an identical workload: 40 panels, spinner titles, sends and mailbox traffic, 30 minutes. Compare 1.0 against this branch with analytics on and with analytics off. The branch must add no measurable main-thread time, keep app CPU within run-to-run noise, and write fewer bytes than 1.0. Run it on Atlas, plus one constrained or low-spec host (see C11-270). Never run the fleet on Hyperion.

## Acceptance
1. From the event log alone, `c11 report` computes foreground hours, workspace names (including closed ones), and the hang rate by load bucket for a multi-day tagged session.
2. Replaying a churned session's log reproduces `c11 tree --all` exactly, with no ghost panels, if item 2 ships.
3. `c11 usage --by panel` matches the transcripts' own counts for a tagged session with at least one Claude and one Codex panel.
4. The performance gate above passes. The result is attached to this ticket.
5. Both toggles and the retention picker work in the real app. With text off, new `panel.input_sent` lines carry no text.
6. The events reference, the skill and the schema are updated, and `scripts/sync-installed-skills.sh` is run.
7. Tests go through the real EventLog and CLI paths, with no source-text assertions.

data.body: Operator decisions 2026-10-06: (1) no full activity-log kill switch in Settings UI; it stays a defaults key documented in the skill. (2) 'Keep message and input text' defaults to on. Both match the description as written.
